name: Mind the Gap: Action Rebinding Attacks against Android GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies action-rebinding attacks in which an Android GUI agent’s planned input is redirected to a different application during the observation–action delay. The evaluation examines cross-application execution and the consequences of treating an earlier screen as the current action target.

name: Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Darwinian Memory splits GUI trajectories into reusable units and updates the memory by retaining useful paths and pruning poor ones. It evaluates this training-free memory mechanism on long multi-application tasks.

name: UI-Mem: Self-Evolving Experience Memory for Online Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UI-Mem stores workflows, skills and failure patterns as reusable templates to guide online GUI reinforcement learning. It varies guidance within rollout groups and continually updates the memory so an unguided policy can learn from guided experiences.

summary: MemGUI-Bench evaluates short-term retention and cross-session experience reuse in mobile GUI agents using paired tasks and repeated-attempt protocols. Its staged evaluator measures memory fidelity, learning and execution efficiency.

name: MobileJailBench: Red Queen Jailbreak Benchmarking for Mobile Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete retained abstract and selected exact-v1 threat-model, construction and evaluation sections. Execution uses a browser-based Android-like simulator, not real Android isolation or live services. The attacker controls instructions and designated carriers, not privileged simulator state/APIs or system/model/harness internals. Rates depend on release, budget and adjudication coverage. SAF labels track observable expressions and actions, not latent reasoning; unresolved episodes are excluded from rate denominators. No independent reproduction.
summary: MobileJailBench evaluates mobile-agent jailbreaks in a browser-based Android-like simulator, combining feedback-driven attack evolution, separately admitted task expansions and evidence-grounded outcome adjudication.

name: MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning-to-Action Security of MLLM-Based Mobile Agents under Cross-Modal Consistency Injection
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 construction, threat-model and evaluation sections. The attacker modifies observation surfaces, not system instructions, model parameters or the OS. State oracles are distinct from emitted-rationale diagnoses, whose labels include outcome-dependent constraints. Those diagnostics are not independent evidence of hidden-reasoning causality. No reproduction or release verification.
summary: MobileInject evaluates visual/textual observation injection in stateful Android workflows using resettable emulators, benign/adversarial state oracles and trace-based diagnosis of emitted rationales and actions.
